# code flow

> A tiny annotation-based workflow engine in Python with a web UI. Workflows
> are plain Python classes with decorated methods — no DSL. This file is a
> complete, accurate reference for LLMs generating or editing flows.

## What a workflow is

Drop a `.py` file anywhere under `workflows/` (subfolders scanned recursively;
each folder on the path is auto-added to the flow's tags; files/folders
starting with `_` are ignored — put shared code in `workflows/_lib/` and
import it as `from _lib.helpers import x`). The folder is re-scanned on every
request, so edits apply without a restart.

```python
from engine import Workflow, start, step, wait

class MyFlow(Workflow):
    description = "Shown in the UI"
    tags = ["billing"]                    # UI grouping/filtering
    inputs = {"amount": 120}              # default inputs, overridable per run
    inputs_schema = {                     # optional: typed inputs -> UI form + validation
        "amount": {"type": "number", "min": 1, "required": True, "help": "order total"},
        "priority": {"type": "select", "options": ["low", "normal", "high"],
                     "default": "normal"},
        # types: string | number | integer | boolean | select | json
        # keys: required, default, min, max, options, help, label
    }
    dashboard = False                     # True => appears in Dashboards tab
    webhook = False                       # True => POST /api/hooks/MyFlow starts it
    # webhook_token = "secret"            # optional per-flow webhook auth

    @start(next="Step1")
    def begin(self, ctx):
        return {"a": 42}                  # returned dicts merge into ctx

    @step(name="Step1", next="Step2", condition="a > 10", retry=3,
          retry_delay=2, retry_backoff=2, retry_on=(ConnectionError,),
          timeout=30, continue_on_error=False)
    def step1(self, ctx):
        self.log("text log line")
        return {"b": ctx["a"] * 2}

    @step(name="Step2", loop="i in items", parallel=4)
    def step2(self, ctx):
        return {"item": ctx["i"], "ok": True}   # per-item result

    @wait(seconds=30, name="Cooldown", next="Done")   # pause, then continue
    def cooldown(self, ctx): pass                     # seconds may be "expr"

    @step(name="Done")
    def done(self, ctx):
        self.outputs({"total": ctx["b"]})     # recorded workflow outputs
```

## Decorator reference

@start(next=None, name=None, retry=0, retry_delay=0, retry_backoff=1,
       retry_on=None, continue_on_error=False, timeout=None)
@step(name=None, next=None, condition=None, loop=None, retry=0, retry_delay=0,
      retry_backoff=1, retry_on=None, continue_on_error=False, timeout=None,
      parallel=1, resumable=False)
@wait(seconds, name=None, next=None, condition=None)

- name: step id referenced by next= (default: function name). Display keeps
  spaces, but derived ctx keys sanitize non-identifier chars to "_":
  step "Fetch Data" -> ctx["Fetch_Data_result"] / _results / _error.
- next: name of the next step; None ends the flow. Runtime branch: return
  {"__next__": "OtherStep"} from a step. Exactly one @start per flow.
- condition: Python expression evaluated against ctx (bare names = ctx keys;
  env available as `env`). Falsy => step SKIPPED, flow continues with next.
- loop: "var in expr" — expr evaluated against ctx once at loop start. Each
  iteration: ctx[var] = item; returned dicts merge into ctx as they complete;
  all results collected in ctx["<Step>_results"] (input order).
- retry/retry_delay/retry_backoff: attempts = retry+1, delay grows
  delay*backoff^(attempt-1). retry_on: exception class/tuple that is
  retryable; other exceptions fail immediately. Retries apply PER loop
  iteration.
- timeout: max seconds per attempt; raises StepTimeoutError (TimeoutError
  subclass). Timed-out call is abandoned, not killed — make it idempotent.
- continue_on_error: after all attempts fail, mark step FAILED but continue
  with next; error stored in ctx["<Step>_error"].
- parallel=N: loop iterations run concurrently on threads, each on a ctx
  SNAPSHOT. Do NOT use running accumulators with parallel; aggregate from
  <Step>_results in the next step. Any failed iteration fails the step.
- resumable=True (sequential loops only): checkpoint each iteration so
  ⏭ resume continues at the failed item. Needs deterministic iterable and
  JSON-serializable results. Incompatible with parallel>1.
- wait: body runs once (dict return merges), then pauses `seconds` (number
  or ctx expression), then next. Cancellable; condition falsy skips pause.

## Workflow instance API (inside steps)

self.log(msg)                        # text line in the step's report
self.log_json(obj, title="")         # pretty JSON block in the report
self.log_table(rows, title="")       # list[dict] -> real table (200-row cap)
self.log_image(src, title="", format="png")  # path | bytes | data-URI |
                                     # matplotlib figure; embeds base64 in the
                                     # report (3MB/img, 20/step)
self.outputs({"k": v})               # merge into workflow outputs
self.widget(type, **props)           # dashboards, see below
self.call_workflow("Other", inputs={...}, env=None)
    # runs child flow synchronously; returns its outputs dict; child gets its
    # own run+report (marked ↳ in history); raises if child fails; inherits
    # parent env unless env="name"; cycles detected; cancel cascades.
self.env                             # selected environment dict (real values)

## Context (ctx) rules

- ctx starts as inputs (class defaults merged with per-run inputs, validated/
  coerced by inputs_schema if present). ctx["env"] = environment dict.
- A step returning a dict merges it into ctx; non-dict return lands in
  ctx["<Step>_result"]. Loops also set ctx["<Step>_results"] (list).
- Keep values JSON-serializable and small: the report's Context section
  truncates >2KB values; resume restores ctx from JSON (non-JSON degrade to
  str). Secret-looking keys (*token*, *secret*, *password*, *api_key*,
  *credential*, *private*) are masked in reports but NOT in self.log lines —
  never log secrets.

## Environments & secrets

environments/*.json — file name = env name, picked per run in the UI/API.
Values may reference OS env vars: "api_token": "${MY_TOKEN}" (resolved at
load; missing var -> warning, placeholder kept). ${}-resolved values and
secret-named keys are masked in UI/reports; steps get real values.
Common flag: "dry_run": true + condition="not env.get('dry_run')".

## Dashboards

Set dashboard=True; steps build widgets with self.widget(...). Refresh in the
Dashboards tab re-runs the flow transiently (no history entry). Input widgets
are generated from inputs_schema (or inferred from inputs defaults).
Widget types: metric(value), stat(value, delta), status(value, status=
ok|warn|err|neutral), progress(value, max), table(rows, format=[...]),
chart(chart=bar|line|area|pie, data=dict|list), list(items), alert(text,
level=info|warn|error), text(text), json(value), html(html), link(url),
section(title). size: "" | "wide" (2 cols) | "full" (row).
Table conditional formatting: format=[{"col": "status", "map": {"paid": "ok"}},
{"col": "amount", "gt": 300, "style": "err"}]; ops eq/ne/gt/gte/lt/lte/
contains; styles ok|warn|err|info|muted; first match wins.

## Failure & resume semantics

- A step fails by RAISING. Run then stops (unless continue_on_error).
- Sequential loop failure: completed iterations' merges are already in ctx;
  <Step>_results is NOT set; remaining items don't run.
- Parallel loop failure: nothing merged (all-or-nothing).
- History actions: ↺ restart (same inputs/env, from the start), ⏭ resume
  (FAILED/CANCELLED/INTERRUPTED: new run starting AT the stopped step with
  ctx restored from history/<id>.resume.json; completed steps shown as
  "carried over"; env re-resolved fresh; failed loop re-runs from item 1
  unless resumable=True).
- Prefer marker pattern for tolerant loops: catch inside the body, return
  {"item": x, "ok": False, "error": str(e)} instead of raising.

## Scheduler & webhooks

Schedules tab / API: {"flow", "type": "interval"|"daily", "every_minutes" |
"time"+"days"(0=Mon..6=Sun), "inputs", "env", "enabled"}. Server-local time;
overlap guard skips a fire while the previous run is still RUNNING.
Webhook: flow sets webhook=True; POST /api/hooks/<Flow> with JSON body as
inputs (?env=, token via X-Webhook-Token or ?token=; per-flow webhook_token
or global CODEFLOW_WEBHOOK_TOKEN).

## REST API (summary — full doc: docs/API.md)

GET  /api/flows                       POST /api/run/<flow> {"inputs", "env"}
GET  /api/runs                        GET  /api/runs/<id>
POST /api/runs/<id>/cancel            POST /api/runs/<id>/restart
POST /api/runs/<id>/resume            DELETE /api/runs/<id> | /api/runs
POST /api/runs/bulk-delete            GET  /api/environments
POST /api/dashboards/<flow>/render    GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/schedules...
POST /api/hooks/<flow>                GET  /reports/<id>  (HTML report)
Statuses: RUNNING SUCCESS FAILED CANCELLED INTERRUPTED (+ step: SKIPPED).
Errors: {"detail": ...}; typed-input failures: 422 with
{"detail": {"message", "errors": {field: msg}}}.

## Config (env vars / .codeflow.env)

CODEFLOW_WORKFLOWS_DIR, CODEFLOW_ENVIRONMENTS_DIR, CODEFLOW_HISTORY_DIR,
CODEFLOW_HISTORY_LIMIT (default 500), CODEFLOW_HOST/PORT (127.0.0.1:8000),
CODEFLOW_WEBHOOK_TOKEN, CODEFLOW_SCHEDULES_FILE. No authentication — keep on
localhost/Tailscale. requests, PyYAML, dirtyjson preinstalled; add more to
requirements.txt.

## Pitfalls (verified behaviors)

- Two steps with the same name=: the second silently wins.
- condition is evaluated BEFORE the step runs, against pre-step ctx.
- Loop iterable evaluated once; mutating it mid-loop misbehaves.
- next= typo -> run fails at that point with "Unknown step"; the flow
  diagram shows a ⚠ node.
- Cycles via next= abort at 1000 steps.
- Parent retry= around call_workflow re-runs the ENTIRE child (multiplies
  with child retries).
- Module top-level code runs on every folder scan — keep it side-effect free.
